title: Hourly to Annual Pay: How Salary Packaging Health Affects Your Take-Home
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using 38-hour weeks, factor in tax, Medicare, and super. Understand salary packaging health and its impact on your pay.
salarySummary: For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours a week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,281.

faqs.q: Does salary packaging health reduce my taxable income for Medicare levy purposes?
faqs.a: Salary packaging health (such as a salary sacrifice arrangement for private health insurance) can reduce your taxable income, which may lower your Medicare levy if your income falls below the reduction thresholds. However, the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate, so this estimate uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. Always check with the Australian Taxation Office for current thresholds.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour for casuals. This loading compensates for lack of paid leave. When converting to annual pay, use the loaded rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks. Super is still paid on top of the loaded rate.

faqs.q: What is the maximum super contribution base and how does it cap my super?
faqs.a: The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary, but only up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (as per the Australian Taxation Office). If your annual earnings exceed that amount, the employer's super obligation stops at the cap. For most workers, this cap does not apply, but high earners should note it.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: The Simple Formula

To convert your hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For example, on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,281 (rounded).

If you are a casual employee, remember to tick the 25% casual loading checkbox on [the timesheet](/) – never enter a rate that already includes loading. The calculator will add it on top.

### Why 38 Hours and 52 Weeks?

The 38-hour week is the standard full-time week under the Fair Work Act. Using 52 weeks gives a consistent annual figure, even though some years have 53 weeks or you may take unpaid leave. This estimate is a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

## Tax and Medicare: What Comes Off Your Annual Pay

Once you have your annual gross, the Australian Taxation Office applies the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on the excess over $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here, so we use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. If your income is below those thresholds, the levy may be reduced or waived.

### Salary Packaging Health and Tax

**Salary packaging health** (e.g., salary sacrificing for private health insurance) can lower your taxable income, potentially moving you into a lower tax bracket or reducing your Medicare levy. However, this article does not deduct salary packaging amounts – it is an estimate only. For a personalised calculation, see [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your gross pay. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year – if your annual earnings exceed that, super stops at the cap. For most workers, this cap does not apply. For example, on the National Minimum Wage annual of $52,281, super would be $6,274 (12% of $52,281).

## Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) – the legal floor for award-free employees.
- **Award rates**: Specific to industries and roles, set by the Fair Work Commission. They are often higher than the minimum wage. Check [pay guides](/blog) for your award.
- **Casual loading**: 25% on top of the base rate, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. This compensates for no paid leave.

Remember, super is paid on top of the loaded rate for casuals.

## Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Check

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time worker on $26.44 per hour, weekly pay is $1,004.90 (38 hours), so fortnightly is $2,009.80 before tax. This helps align with common pay cycles.

## Using the Reference Tables

For more precise conversions, see our [reference tables](/data) which show annual equivalents for various hourly rates. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page explains the formula in detail.

### A Note on Averages

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. That is an average, not a median for any specific job. Total earnings for all employees (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week. Do not use these averages as a substitute for your own rate.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a full interactive tool, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate. Check the casual loading box if applicable, and see your annual, fortnightly, and take-home estimates.
